The result? You are left scrambling, calling every contact you have, while dirty utensils pile up and the house descends into chaos.

MyBuddyMaid was built to solve this exact problem. We operate a structured, technology-driven maid placement service that connects Indian families with police-verified, trained domestic helpers. We do not just send you the first person available; we match you with a maid whose skills, language, and schedule align with your household's specific needs.

Whether you live in a 1 BHK apartment in Pune or a sprawling villa in Hyderabad, whether you are a young couple who just needs someone for a few hours in the morning or a joint family that requires all-day support — we have a plan that fits. Our part-time maids can handle daily cleaning, utensil washing, and laundry in as little as two to four hours. And if your maid does not work out, our one-year replacement guarantee ensures you get a new match at no extra cost. No more begging neighbours for contacts. No more compromising on trust. tasks.detail: Thorough sweeping and wet-mopping of all rooms, hallways, and balconies using appropriate cleaners for marble, vitrified tiles, wooden flooring, and mosaic surfaces. Includes moving lightweight furniture to clean underneath.

Hand-washing delicate garments, loading and unloading the washing machine, hanging clothes to dry on the balcony or terrace, and neatly folding and organizing dried clothes in wardrobes.

Making beds every morning, fluffing pillows, and changing bed sheets, pillow covers, and mattress protectors on a weekly schedule or as needed.
Pressing clothes using a steam or dry iron, hanging formal wear on hangers, folding casual clothing, and organizing wardrobes seasonally — packing away winter or summer clothes as appropriate.
Collecting garbage from all rooms, segregating wet and dry waste as per municipal guidelines, and handing over trash to the building's collection system or municipal pickup.
Receiving grocery deliveries from BigBasket, Zepto, or Blinkit, checking items against the order list, and stocking them properly in the pantry, fridge, or designated storage areas.
Cleaning the pooja room or mandir area, wiping idols gently, replacing old flowers, and maintaining the cleanliness of prayer items — handled with appropriate cultural sensitivity.
Preparing the home before guests arrive — extra mopping, arranging guest bedrooms, cleaning the guest bathroom, laying out fresh towels, and a general tidying of common areas.
For homes with pets — cleaning pet feeding bowls, sweeping pet hair from sofas and floors, wiping paw prints from entryways, and maintaining the pet sleeping area.

But here is the uncomfortable truth that many Indian households face today: nobody has the time or energy to cook three meals a day, seven days a week. The romanticised image of a home-cooked thali with six items, fresh roti, and homemade pickle is wonderful — but who is actually making it when both spouses leave for work at 8 AM and return at 8 PM?

For years, the fallback was ordering food from Swiggy or Zomato. And while food delivery is convenient, it is also expensive, unpredictable in quality, and — let us be honest — not something you want to feed your children or elderly parents every single day. Restaurant food is loaded with oil, salt, and flavour enhancers that are fine occasionally but terrible for long-term health. Indian families are increasingly aware of this, which is why the demand for personal home cooks has skyrocketed.

But finding a good cook in India is harder than finding a good maid. A maid's work is visible — you can see if the floor is clean. A cook's work involves hygiene practices you cannot always see, taste preferences that are deeply personal, and nutritional awareness that matters for your family's health. A bad cook does not just mean bad food — it means wasted groceries, an unhappy family, and potential health issues.

MyBuddyMaid's Cook Service addresses all of these challenges. We maintain a curated roster of cooks who specialize in different cuisines — from the rich gravies and rotis of North Indian cooking to the dosas, idlis, and sambars of South Indian kitchens. Every cook is police-verified, hygiene-trained, and matched to your family's specific dietary needs. intro:
The first 40 days after childbirth — known as the 'confinement period' or 'japa' in many Indian cultures — are among the most demanding and overwhelming weeks a woman will ever experience. Your body is recovering from the physical trauma of delivery (whether vaginal or C-section), your hormones are in complete upheaval, you are surviving on fragmented sleep with a newborn who needs feeding every two hours, and you are expected to figure out breastfeeding, swaddling, burping, and a dozen other newborn care skills — all while dealing with post-delivery pain, stitches, and emotional vulnerability.

In traditional Indian families, this period was managed by the extended family. The new mother's mother or mother-in-law would move in, take charge of the kitchen, manage the newborn's bath and massage, prepare special postpartum foods (gond ke laddu, ajwain water, haldi milk), and ensure the new mother rested and recovered. This support system was the backbone of postpartum recovery for centuries. But today, this safety net is fraying. Nuclear families mean the new mother's parents may live in a different city. Working mothers-in-law may not be able to take extended time off. And even well-meaning family members may rely on outdated practices that conflict with modern paediatric advice.

The consequences of inadequate postnatal support are serious. Postpartum depression affects nearly 1 in 5 Indian mothers, and the risk is significantly higher when the mother feels unsupported, overwhelmed, and isolated. Breastfeeding failure rates are high in the first few weeks when new mothers do not have proper latching guidance. Newborns are vulnerable to infections, colic, and jaundice — conditions that need early detection by someone experienced. And C-section recovery requires careful wound management and restricted movement that is nearly impossible to maintain when you are also the primary caretaker of a newborn.

MyBuddyMaid's Postnatal Care Service bridges this gap with trained, experienced caregivers who specialize exclusively in postpartum mother and newborn care. Our postnatal caregivers — many of whom are experienced mothers themselves — handle everything from traditional oil massage (maalish) for the mother and baby, to breastfeeding position guidance, to preparing nutritious recovery meals, to managing the newborn's complete daily routine. They bring the wisdom of traditional Indian postnatal practices combined with awareness of modern medical guidelines. Whether you need someone for just the first 40 days or an extended 3-month support period, we ensure that both mother and baby are cared for with expertise and warmth.

Being a calm, reassuring presence during the emotionally volatile postpartum period.
